subject: Post-demo follow-up: model mix, token scenarios, and unit-cost targets
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@novafirm.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novafirm.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: model mix, token scenarios, and unit-cost targets

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the productive demo earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size a pilot that matches your budget and performance goals.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary UX: live chat + context summarization for customer success agents (high chat tokens).
- Secondary workload: nightly embeddings of support docs + semantic search (high vector ops, lower token volume).
- Experimental/occasional reranking on search results (small fractional traffic).

Open asks (can you confirm these so we scope cost scenarios?):
1) Expected monthly token volume (approximate): total tokens / month. If unsure, give low/typical/high ranges.
2) Desired target unit-economics: what target $/1M tokens would make sense for your procurement budget?
3) Per-model split: estimate what percent of total tokens you expect to go to each class: chat (LLM gen), embeddings (vectorization calls), rerank/rescore.

Attached a quick workbook (novafirm_model_mix_scenarios.xlsx) with three unit-econ scenarios and placeholders — fill the blue cells and send back. I also attached the demo recording for your team.

Preliminary assumptions we used in the workbook:
- Chat model: mix of 8k-context chat and 2k chat variants; embeddings: 1536-d vectors; rerank uses short-context encoder.
- Baseline latency SLOs: 300–500ms P95 for agent-facing chat.

Rough unit-econ buckets (high-level, back-of-envelope):
- Conservative (no batching/hosted peak pricing): ~$1,400 / 1M tokens
- Optimized (batching + cache + mixed precision): ~$800 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated reserved (customer-dedicated pools, sustained load): ~$520 / 1M tokens

If you can reply with the three items above by EOD Tue (PST), we’ll pull together a recommended pilot scope (model variants, token caps, pilot duration) and an estimated price band for procurement.

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm volumes and target $/1M tokens + any compliance must-haves
- Us: return a 3-option pilot proposal and a mutually agreed mutual action plan (MAP) with dates

Thanks — glad we’re aligned on priorities.

—
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: novafirm_model_mix_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet), MADP_demo_recording.mp4 (video)

From: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@novafirm.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: model mix, token scenarios, and unit-cost targets

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap and the workbook. Quick answers below (we gave ranges where helpful):

1) Estimated monthly volumes (total tokens, first 6 months):
- Low: ~50M tokens/mo
- Typical: ~150M tokens/mo
- High (growth): ~400M tokens/mo

2) Target unit-cost: our procurement target is roughly $750–$950 / 1M tokens. If you can show an optimized path to <$900 that would be ideal for our finance team.

3) Per-model split (percentage of tokens):
- Chat (agent-facing generative): 70%
- Embeddings (vectorize documents + occasional re-embed): 25% (vectors: ~600k vectors/mo estimated)
- Rerank/rescore: 5%

Notes/asks: embedding pricing is a separate line in our budget — can you include a quick note on per-vector cost (or a guidance if that's included in token buckets)? Also curious what assumptions you used to get to the $800/$1,400 numbers — are those mostly GPU-hour + vCPU overhead or do they assume caching/prefix reuse?

We can aim to fill your blue cells and get that back to you by Tue EOD. If you can also attach the short unit-econ writeup (one-pager) that'd be helpful for procurement.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Product — Novafirm
alyssa@novafirm.com | +1 212-555-0987

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@novafirm.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: model mix, token scenarios, and unit-cost targets

Alyssa — thanks for the quick numbers, super helpful. Looping in Marissa (pricing) and Soojin (solutions) so we can turn this into concrete scenarios and a MAP.

Short answers to your questions: the bucketed $/1M numbers are blended estimates that include GPU runtime, memory pressure (KV cache), orchestration overhead, and expected batching/caching benefits. Embeddings are priced separately in the proposal but we show a blended line-item in the workbook so you can see total spend. For per-vector guidance: on common 1536-d embeddings we size ~ $0.08–$0.30 per 1k vectors depending on throughput and retention (hot vs cold).

Proposed three scenarios (ballpark — we will formalize in the attached one-pager "unit_econ_scenarios.pdf"):

- Scenario A — On-demand hosted (no reserved capacity)
  - Assumptions: low batching, conservative cache hit-rate, mixed model variants
  - Estimated blended unit-cost: ~$1,350 / 1M tokens
  - Embedding: $0.25 / 1k vectors
- Scenario B — Optimized hosted (batching + prefix/KV cache + model mix tuning)
  - Assumptions: 30–40% effective batching, 60% cache reuse on repeated context, tuned quantized weights where supported
  - Estimated blended unit-cost: ~$820 / 1M tokens
  - Embedding: $0.12 / 1k vectors
- Scenario C — Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit)
  - Assumptions: reserved GPU fleet, sustained utilization > 60%, near-linear unit improvements from longer-lived KV cache and aggressive batching
  - Estimated blended unit-cost: ~$540 / 1M tokens

Suggested mutual action plan (MAP) for a pilot:
1) Week 0: sign NDA/POC SOW (1–2 pages) — agree on pilot success metrics (cost, P95 latency, quality eval set)
2) Week 1–2: ingest sample corpus, instrument token counting + eval prompts
3) Week 3–6: run pilot at scaled-down traffic (10–25% of expected) across Scenario B config
4) Week 7: review quality metrics and billing simulation, decide on upgrade to Dedicated if economics justify

Next steps from us by Tue: a one-page unit-econ summary (attached) and a filled workbook with the three scenario sheets completed.

Marissa / Soojin — any additions on pricing cadence or procurement paperwork?

—
Karthik

From: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@novafirm.com>

This looks good to us. We’ll aim to: (a) populate the workbook with our ranges by Tue EOD, and (b) move forward with the MAP for Scenario B pilot (3–6 weeks).

Tom and I will review the one-pager with procurement and revert with any SOW or PO questions. Can you tentatively block a quick sync next Wed to kick off the pilot if procurement gives the go-ahead?

Thanks — looking forward to the proposal.

Best,
Alyssa
